claims: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
The Challenger orbiter broke apart 73 seconds into its 25th flight (STS-51L).
The Challenger orbiter broke apart at approximately 46,000 feet.
The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster killed all seven crew members.
The failure was caused by O-ring seals in the right solid rocket booster failing due to cold weather.
The failure resulted in a catastrophic explosion.
This video shows the launch and the immediate aftermath of the Challenger disaster.
